sources.entry: pyright - Full-featured static type checker for Python from Microsoft, the engine behind Pylance.

summary.one_liner: Pyright is a standards-based static type checker for Python from Microsoft, shipped as a command-line tool and a Visual Studio Code extension.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Pyright as a full-featured, standards-based static type checker for Python, designed for high performance and for use on large codebases. It includes a command-line tool and an extension for Visual Studio Code. The README links to an in-browser Pyright Playground for trying it out. Documentation covers installation, configuration, and usage, and is referenced rather than reproduced in the README. It also mentions a weekly benchmark comparing Pyright with other Python type checkers, and a release history tracking per-package execution time and peak memory. An environment variable, PYRIGHT_TMPDIR, lets users override the temp directory root when the default is missing or unwritable.
use_cases: find type errors before running code
check type annotations in large Python projects
type checking inside Visual Studio Code
run type checks in CI or the command line
try type checking in a browser
how_to_run: Refer to the documentation for installation, configuration, and usage details (not included in the README).
notable: Standards-based type checking designed for high performance on large codebases
Ships as both a command-line tool and a Visual Studio Code extension
Engine behind Pylance, per the awesome-python listing
Browser-based Pyright Playground for trying it out
Environment variable PYRIGHT_TMPDIR for overriding the temp directory in remote or server environments
caveats: Installation and configuration details are only in external documentation, not in the README
Core type checking is tied to Pyright; language service features are associated with the separate Pylance project
License not named in the README
